chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rib'i from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I said to him, 'Can a man move backwards while he is in the prayer?' He said, 'No'. I said, 'So can he move forward?' He said, 'Yes, whatever he desires to, towards the Qiblah'.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to move forward or backward during Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the fiqh of row alignment (saff), specifically permitting a worshipper to advance forward toward the Qiblah to join the line, while generally prohibiting moving backward. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining orderly congregational prayer and correcting one's position relative to the Imam without breaking the prayer's validity. It highlights the practical flexibility allowed in adjusting one's place within the saff to ensure proper formation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I said to himasws, ‘Can the man move backwards while he is in the Salāt?’ Heasws said: ‘No’. I said, ‘So can he move forward?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, whatever he so desire to, towards the Qiblah’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib‘i from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Can a man move backward in Salah (prayer)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot do so.’ I then asked, ‘Can he move forward?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, as much as he wants to al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah).’”
